# `nlink-lab conntrack`

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
List a lab's tracked flows (its nodes' conntrack tables), or delete them with `--flush`.

Filters select by the flow's original direction, as it began (`--dst` is the address before a DNAT); every filter given must hold. The NAT REPLY column shows where a translated flow's replies come from. Deleting a flow makes its next packet start a new one, through the rules as they are now: what `apply` does for the flows of the NAT rules it changes.

JSON OUTPUT (with `--json`): { "schema_version": 1, "lab": str, "flows": [ { "node": str, "family": "ipv4" | "ipv6", "proto": str, "orig": { "src", "dst", "sport", "dport" }, "reply": { … }, "state": str?, "status": [str], "timeout": int?, "mark": int?, "zone": int? }, ... ], "deleted": { NODE: int } }  (with --flush) Schema: docs/json-schemas/conntrack.schema.json. With `--quiet`, the number of flows listed or deleted.

Usage: nlink-lab conntrack [OPTIONS] [NODE]

Arguments:
  [NODE]
          Only this node's flows. Default: every node

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

      --proto <PROTO>
          Only this protocol: tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, sctp, … or a number

      --src <ADDR>
          Only flows from this source (an address or a CIDR), as they began

      --dst <ADDR>
          Only flows to this destination (an address or a CIDR), as they began: before a DNAT

      --sport <PORT>
          Only this source port (with --proto tcp or udp)

      --dport <PORT>
          Only this destination port (with --proto tcp or udp)

      --mark <MARK>
          Only flows with this connection mark

      --zone <ZONE>
          Only flows in this conntrack zone

      --status <STATUS>
          Only flows with these status bits (comma-separated): snat, dnat, assured, seen-reply, confirmed, expected, dying

      --flush
          Delete the flows selected (every flow, without a filter) instead of listing them. Their next packet starts a new flow, through the rules as they are now

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
